1300.author: HongyeZhou
1300.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal analysis, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

An artifact version's number is taken from `artifact.currentVersion + 1` and pushed into the catalog with no uniqueness guard. Every later lookup by `(artifactId, version)` uses `.find()`, so two records sharing a number would not raise anything — the first match silently wins. Because the UI labels versions by number alone (`v3`), a duplicate would be indistinguishable to the user while the server returns whichever record it finds first.

**Why it is worth a guard, even though it is hard to reach**

Normal writes are already serialized: `store.ts:5791` assigns the number from `artifact.currentVersion`, there is no `await` between the base-version check and the push, and a stale base is rejected with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_CONFLICT`. So two ordinary writes cannot collide.

The paths that are *not* covered:

- Snapshot restore re-registers versions through the same call (`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1267` passes `restorationIds`, and the number is still derived from the target artifact's `currentVersion`). Restoring into a project that already has an artifact with the same `logicalName` is exactly the case where two writers describe the same artifact.
- More than one API process opening the same `catalog_state` row. The whole catalog is one JSON document (`store.ts:1547`), so SQLite cannot be asked for a unique index on `(artifactId, version)` — the guard has to be in code.
- Any future importer that copies versions verbatim instead of appending.

**What a duplicate does to the rest of the system**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/artifact-labels.ts:56` — `isNewer` falls back to `createdAt` when the numbers are equal, so ordering is only as good as the timestamps; the "current version" the list shows can be the older content.
- `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:18` — `listProjectArtifactVersions(...).find(v => v.version === input.version)` returns the first match, so restoring "version 3" can write the other version 3's bytes into the workspace.
- `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:260` — dependency resolution does the same by number, so provenance could bind to the wrong record.
- `store.ts:5638` (`latestReportVersion`) sorts by number and takes `[0]`.

None of these raise; the wrong bytes just come back.

**What I tried, and did not reproduce** (`zh-CN`, desktop web surface)

1. Same session, same path rewritten twice → `v1`/`v2`/`v3`, no duplicates.
2. Two subagents told to append to the same `/workspace/report.md` simultaneously → one new `v3` containing both appends (a second attempt had them create `report-A.md` / `report-B.md` instead).

So this is not reachable through the UI today; it is a missing invariant, not a live user-facing bug.

**Suggested fix** (chosen by the reporter: enforce uniqueness server-side)

1. Allocate the number from the catalog rather than from a field that can drift:
   ```ts
   const next = Math.max(0, ...this.catalog.artifactVersions
     .filter((v) => v.artifactId === artifact.id)
     .map((v) => v.version)) + 1;
   ```
2. Before `this.catalog.artifactVersions.push(version)` (`store.ts:5801`), reject the write if that `(artifactId, next)` already exists — `ARTIFACT_VERSION_DUPLICATE`, same shape as the existing `ARTIFACT_VERSION_CONFLICT`.
3. On load (`store.ts:1370`, where the catalog is already re-validated and `currentVersion` is recomputed at `store.ts:5833`), detect duplicates once and make them unambiguous before serving — renumbering by `createdAt` keeps every record reachable; a hard failure keeps the data pristine but stops the service.
4. A regression test for 1–2 next to `store.test.ts:3585` (where "server forces auto-increment" is already asserted).

Step 3 is the one judgement call: renumber silently, or refuse to load until a human looks. Either way the check should exist; the alternative — today's behaviour — is a wrong file restored with no trace.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery, `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21); API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser for the reproduction attempts: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- No screenshot: the defect is in storage/lookup, and the interface would only show its consequence.

### Additional Information

- Found while walking the artifact feature area (D7-03 版本切换): the picker offers `v3`/`v2`/`v1` with no other identifier, which is what makes a duplicate invisible rather than confusing-but-solvable.
- Related, separate: the panel/width and run-failure issues are #1296 and #1292; this one touches neither.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
1300.title: [Bug]: Artifact version numbers are allocated without a uniqueness guard

1302.author: HongyeZhou
1302.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** In the desktop app, a report's citation chip (for example `[evidence1]`) opens the 科学记忆 card. When the memory graph cannot answer — the sidecar is restarting, or it refuses the query with its 503 budget limit — the card correctly says "暂时读不到科学记忆 / 记忆服务没有响应。稍后再试一次。", but the **only action it offers is "打开科学记忆设置" (Open scientific memory settings)**. The wording invites a retry; the UI has no retry. To get the content the reader has to close the card and press the citation again.

**Steps to reproduce.**

1. Desktop app, memory graph enabled, and a report whose body cites evidence (a chip such as `[evidence1]`).
2. Make the memory graph unavailable: stop the memory-graph sidecar, or let it refuse with its 503 budget limit, so `POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type` answers `{"hits":[],"total":0,"truncated":false,"reason":"memory_graph_unreachable"}`.
3. Press the `[evidence1]` chip in the report.

**Expected.** The card offers "重试" (retry), which re-reads this reference in place; once the service is back, pressing it shows the evidence without closing the card.

**Actual.** The card shows the unreachable message and its only button is "打开科学记忆设置" — a settings page that cannot affect a transient outage (and that may even read "运行正常" at that moment, because its status line reads the unauthenticated `/api/health`). No retry is offered anywhere in the card.

**Why (code, main).** `apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx`:

- `:170-177` — `memory_graph_disabled` → `{ offerSettings: true }`
- `:183-190` — `memory_graph_unreachable` / `memory_graph_query_limit` → `{ offerSettings: true }`
- `:195-203` — the request failed outright → `{ offerSettings: true }`
- `:268-270` — the action is one ternary over that flag:
  `action={state.offerSettings ? TEXT.memory.openSettings : TEXT.memory.retry}` and
  `onAction={state.offerSettings ? onOpenSettings : () => setAttempt((v) => v + 1)}`

Because every error state sets `offerSettings: true`, the `重试` label and the `setAttempt` re-read path are unreachable — `attempt` never changes, so the effect never runs again.

**Impact.** Transient unavailability is a normal state (sidecar restart, query budget refusal), yet the only recovery is to close the card and press the citation again. The card's own sentence ("稍后再试一次") promises an action the UI does not provide.

**Suggested fix (not a prescription).** Give the action to the state rather than to one flag: `disabled` keeps "打开科学记忆设置"; `unreachable` / `query_limit` / request-failure render "重试" (the existing `setAttempt` path), optionally with "打开科学记忆设置" as a secondary link.

**Screenshots.** Both are the same card at two error states; the action button sits at the same place in both.

A — memory graph unreachable (the bug):

![A: unreachable — the only action is Open settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb7620cd-de7a-4bf6-bc4a-676640feb011)

B — single card, unreachable, button highlighted:

![B: unreachable card, button highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ded64ffe-b0fc-4a56-ae8c-134a0580c252)

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Desktop web surface (`apps/desktop`) served at `http://127.0.0.1:5174` from a checkout of `main` at the SHA below; Linux x64 host, Chromium 1228, viewport 1500×950, `zh-CN`.
- Backend in the same host: API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `4411`; memory graph sidecar with the `local` backend on `127.0.0.1:17675`; 科学记忆 enabled.
- No cloud model is needed to reproduce — the card fails before any model call. The report used for the screenshots contains two evidence citations.
- Stopping only the sidecar is enough; the API and the rest of the app stay up.

### Additional Information

- Reproducible with the sidecar's 503 budget refusal as well (`reason: memory_graph_query_limit`), which the code already treats as a temporary failure rather than a missing record — so the retry is meaningful in exactly the case the card refuses to offer it.
- The three error states are distinguishable in the code (`disabled` vs `temporarily unavailable` vs request failure); only the action collapses them into one.
- Related but separate: the settings page's status line reads the unauthenticated `/api/health`, so it can report "运行正常" while every query is refused; that is a different report.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-22T01:36:38Z).
- Affected file: `apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx` (lines 170-177, 183-190, 195-203, 268-270).
- Evidence captured 2026-11-22 on that SHA.
1302.title: [Bug]: Citation card offers no Retry when the memory graph is temporarily unavailable

1303.author: HongyeZhou
1303.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

`Settings › Timeouts › Execution timeout` has no effect on an ordinary agent shell run. The panel says "The longest one code execution in the sandbox may take.", 5 seconds were saved, and `sleep 10; echo done` still ran to completion.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open `Settings › Timeouts`, set **Execution timeout** to `5` seconds, save (the row reports `Saved`).
2. Start a new session and ask the agent to run `sleep 10; echo done` in the sandbox.
3. The tool returns `done` with exit code 0 after ~18 s of wall time; nothing is interrupted.

![Execution timeout set to 5 seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66ec1a15-6f83-488d-a6bd-ee76a58f093c)

![The 10-second command completes under a 5-second limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4f35b10-c721-40ce-b24d-dd5fbbecbef4)

**The value does reach the run**

The shell record the API persists for that execution carries `originalExecutionContext.executionTimeoutMs = 5000`, and the execution itself spans `2026-11-22T06:36:15.839Z → 2026-11-22T06:36:26.045Z` (10.2 s, `succeeded`). So this is not a settings-plumbing problem: the request was correctly bounded and the bound was dropped afterwards.

**Root cause**

`services/runner/src/server.ts:1027` overwrites the request's limit for every managed (non-direct) execution:

```ts
// A client's waiting deadline is not the process's lifetime, so managed
// executions run without one by default. An operator who explicitly set
// SCIENCE_AGENT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS still gets a lifetime bound; ...
if (!direct) execution.executionTimeoutMs = config.execTimeoutMs > 0 ? config.execTimeoutMs : 0;
```

`config.execTimeoutMs` comes only from the Runner's environment (`server.ts:340`, `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS`), whose default is `0` (`services/runner/src/executor.ts:100`, "unlimited"). A Runner started without that variable logs `execution timeout: unlimited` and therefore forces every request to `0`.

The setting is not a client waiting deadline: it is the deployment's own limit. The API sends it as `executionTimeoutMs` from the system setting `runnerExecTimeoutMs` (`services/api/src/configuration/settings-catalog.ts:26`) at `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:1423` and `:1966`, and the desktop text describes exactly that meaning (`apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:1581`).

**Impact**

- `pnpm install`, a model download or a long training loop runs to the end regardless of the configured limit — the one thing an operator sets to bound sandbox time does nothing.
- The localized timeout failure already exists (`runner_exec`: `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:2090`, `Tool execution exceeded N seconds…`) but cannot be reached from this setting.
- A user who lowers the limit to stop runaway commands gets no feedback that their change had no effect.

**Suggested fix**

Treat both sides as limits and keep the stricter one (0 meaning unlimited on either side):

```ts
const requested = execution.executionTimeoutMs ?? 0;
const configured = config.execTimeoutMs;
execution.executionTimeoutMs = requested > 0 && configured > 0
  ? Math.min(requested, configured)
  : Math.max(requested, configured);
```

If the Runner-side variable is deliberately the only authority, then the settings panel must say so (or the field must stop being offered as editable) and the API should stop sending a value that is discarded. Either way, add a regression test where a managed execution is submitted with `executionTimeoutMs: 5000` and a `sleep 10` payload must be terminated — the existing executor tests around `services/runner/src/scientific-execution.test.ts` are the natural place.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411` (started without `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS`), desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2, bubblewrap sandbox (`bbdbdd5c`).
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Runner startup banner for this instance: `execution timeout: unlimited`.

### Additional Information

- Found while fault-injecting an execution limit for scenario S-203 (fault recovery).
- Related but separate: #1300 (artifact version numbers without a uniqueness guard), #1299 (model connection test localization).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
1303.title: [Bug]: The Execution timeout setting does not bound a sandboxed shell run

1304.author: HongyeZhou
1304.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A successful run ends with a "用时 N 秒" line. A run that fails while the model is still being reached ends with the failure card and nothing else — no duration at all. The run does know how long it took; the line just lives somewhere that never renders on this path.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Make the selected model unreachable (point its base URL at a dead port, or stop the model service) and send any message in a new session.
2. The run stops with `模型服务连接失败`, the explanation "无法连接模型服务，运行已停止。建议检查网络、代理设置及模型服务地址后重试。" and a folded "技术详情".
3. Nothing says how long the attempt took, although the same conversation's successful runs show `用时 N 秒` under the fold line.

![A failed run: title, explanation and technical details, but no elapsed time](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd10a991-217f-4147-a660-a645f234bcb1)

**Root cause**

The duration is produced only by the fold line of a run, and the fold line only exists when the run has something to fold:

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AssistantTurn.tsx:605` — `const fold = live || hasMiddleContent(run, shown);`
- `hasMiddleContent` (`:452-465`) requires reasoning, subagents, tool calls, or prose beyond the shown answer. A run that fails before the model answers has none of them, so `fold` is `false` and the `<details>` block is skipped entirely.
- The elapsed label itself is built in `foldLabel` (`:469-482`) from `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(run.finishedAt - run.startedAt)` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:360`) and rendered only inside that `<summary>` (`:634-655`).
- The failure card is rendered separately (`:379`, `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx:31`) from `code`, `message` and `timeout` — no timing is passed to it.

So a failed run with no foldable content can never display a duration, even though `run.startedAt` and `run.finishedAt` are both known.

**Impact**

- A failure that took 4 minutes after retries looks exactly like one that failed instantly; the user cannot tell whether time was spent in the model gateway, in a retry loop, or nowhere.
- Anything that reads `用时` to recognise a finished run (a person skimming, or an automated check) sees no end marker on failed runs.
- The information is present in state, so this is a rendering gap rather than missing data.

**Suggested fix**

Render the duration for every terminal run that has both timestamps, independent of the fold:

- pass `startedAt`/`finishedAt` into `RunFailureCard` and add the same `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(...)` line there, or
- render a standalone `run-duration` line next to the failure card when `fold === false` and both timestamps exist.

A desktop unit test asserting that a terminal run with `startedAt`/`finishedAt` and no turns still shows the elapsed line would keep this from regressing.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- The failing run: the selected model's base URL was unreachable, so the run stopped before producing any turn — which is exactly the case with nothing to fold.

### Additional Information

- Found while fault-injecting a broken model in scenario S-203 (fault recovery): the missing duration made it impossible to tell from the transcript whether the run had ended at all.
- Related but separate: #1292 (the failure code and detail text for this same card), #1299 (model connection test localization), #1300 (artifact version numbers).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
1304.title: [Bug]: A failed run shows no elapsed time

1305.author: HongyeZhou
1305.body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **Summary** The approval card is mixed-language: the eyebrow and the buttons are Chinese, while the one line that says what is about to be authorized is a hard-coded English sentence. ``` 需要权限 Run a shell script in the Session workspace <- English, from the server workspace-code <- resource id [仅允许一次] [允许同类操作] [拒绝] <- Chinese, from the client ``` ![The permission card: Chinese heading and buttons around an English summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a489fefc-8fa8-4441-baa8-0695105e1463) **Steps to reproduce** 1. Language zh-CN, permission mode "请求批准" (ask for approval). 2. Ask the agent to run any shell command in the session workspace. 3. The approval card appears with the English summary above. **Root cause** `apps/desktop/src/views/PermissionCard.tsx:58` renders the summary verbatim: ```tsx {TEXT.permission.required}

{request.summary}

``` and the server builds `summary` as an English sentence. Every approval path does this, not only the shell one: - `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:297` — `Run a shell script …` - `:623` — `Run Python code …`, `:786` — `Run ${language} code …` - `:398` — the `DIRECT HOST EXECUTION: Runner …, account …, No sandbox filesystem, process or network isolation; …` warning - `:526` — `Copy N selected files between authorized Workspaces` - `:555`, `:576` — NPU job cancel/run - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts:333` — `Call repaired MCP tool …`, `:554` — `tool call` - `services/api/src/agent-run/sandbox-network-consent.ts:52` — `Sandbox network on … for this Agent run: …` The action and resource fields (`code`, `workspace-code`) are raw identifiers by design and are acceptable as such; the summary is prose and is not translated anywhere. **Impact** - This is the sentence a user must understand before granting shell, Python or **direct host** execution. A Chinese-reading user sees the button labels but not the scope being granted, so approving becomes a reflex — and the direct-host warning (no filesystem, process or network isolation; host credentials reachable; effects not reversible) is the most consequential text in the product. - It makes an otherwise fully localized surface look broken, and the same card is used in the walkthrough that a reviewer sees on a screenshot. - It also affects matching consent: "允许同类操作" scopes a broader grant, and the user cannot check what "同类" means because the description is unreadable. **Suggested fix** Send structured fields instead of a finished English sentence, and let the client compose the text from its own catalog: e.g. `{ kind: "shell" | "python" | "language" | "file-copy" | "npu-run" | "mcp-tool" | "network", target, scope, hosts?, language?, remoteHostAlias? }`, with the current English string kept as a fallback for builds that cannot render the structured form. Where the API must stay the source of truth (the direct-host warning), translate by the request's locale, which the API already knows from the session's language preference. Whichever route is taken, the direct-host warning deserves its own copy pass: it is several sentences of consequences and should be readable, not just shorter. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`. - Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2. - Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`, permission mode "请求批准". - Observed on `run_shell` in the session workspace (resource `workspace-code`); the same rendering path is shared by every tool that asks for approval. ### Additional Information - Found while fault-injecting approval requirements for scenario S-203 (fault recovery). - The same untranslated-summary shape appears in the run failure card (#1292) and the model connection test (#1299) from the same round of testing; this issue is specifically about the approval card. ### Version Information - Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main` - Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21) - Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
1305.title: [Bug]: The approval card title stays English in a Chinese interface

1306.author: HongyeZhou
1306.body:
﻿### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A product declared in a brand-new conversation can silently continue the version chain of an artifact created in an older conversation: the new session receives `version 4` of an artifact it never created, the older session's product is overwritten with the new content, and neither the user nor the model is told that this happened.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In session A, ask the agent to write `report.md` in the workspace and declare it as an artifact. It becomes `v1`; publish two revisions so it reaches `v3`.
2. Start a new session B in the same project and ask the agent to write a different `report.md` (this is a separate piece of work — a run log, not a revision of A's report).
3. The agent calls `declare_artifact` with only `{"path": "report.md", ...}`.
4. B's answer says `Artifact 0635ff24…, version 4`, and B's artifact panel lists `report.md` at `v4`. Open session A: its `report.md` is now that same `v4`, carrying B's content.

**What the data shows** (`main` `bbdbdd5c`, `zh-CN`, desktop web surface)

Session B's `/api/sessions/<B>/artifact-outputs` returns exactly one entry:

```
artifact.id            0635ff24-0d7e-4eb2-a253-253d28f5e624
artifact.createdInSessionId     fca861a5-…   (session A)
artifact.createdInSessionTitle  用 Python 创建 report.md 文件
artifact.currentVersion 4
version.sessionId       e9afb9af-…   (session B)
version.version         4
version.turnId          set
```

Session A's `/api/sessions/<A>/artifacts` now reports the same artifact with `currentVersion: 4` and `updatedAt: 2026-11-22T06:41:49.242Z` — the moment session B published. So A's artifact row is visible, and its content has been replaced by another conversation's work.

**Why it happens**

- `services/api/src/store.ts:5752-5755` — when the caller does not pass an `artifactId`, the target artifact is resolved by `(projectId, name, research scope)`. A same-named artifact in the same project, created by *another session*, is a valid target.
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5797` — the new version takes `artifact.currentVersion + 1`, so the first product of a fresh conversation is `v4`.
- The publish result handed back to the model contains only `artifact_id`, `name`, `content`, `origin`, `version` and `version_id` — no `createdInSessionId`, no title, no previous version. The model therefore believes it declared a new artifact and reports "version 4" to the user without being able to explain `v1`–`v3`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:378-400` — the version menu labels entries `v{version}` only; there is no session or timestamp, and the picker is only rendered when a session produced more than one version (so in session B there is no picker at all, just `v4`).
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5728` already refuses cross-session rewrites with a 409 — `请在当前研究会话中创建独立产物，不能改写另一个研究副本` — but only when the owning session is a *research copy*. Two ordinary sessions of the same project are allowed to write over each other without any confirmation.
- When the caller passes no `baseVersionId`, the CAS check at `store.ts:5746` is skipped, so the write does not even need to have seen the version it overwrites.

**Impact**

- A fresh conversation's first deliverable starts at `v4`, relative to history the user cannot see in that conversation. Nothing in the panel says where `v1`–`v3` came from.
- The older conversation's product changes underneath it, silently. A user reopening it sees different content at a new version number with no record of which session wrote it.
- The model can "update" a product it has never read, and will describe a foreign version chain as its own work.
- Two sessions writing the same name interleave versions, and without `baseVersionId` the last write wins with no conflict raised. Version-number collisions are a separate defect (#1300, fixed by #1301); this one is about *which* chain a write lands in.
- Cleanup is asymmetric: `store.ts:5579` authorizes `deleteArtifact` against the *creating* session, so the session that can see and revise the artifact is not necessarily the one that may delete it.

**Suggested fix** (approved direction: make the continuation visible, and ask before the first cross-session write)

1. **Disclose the continuation.** Return the origin in the publish result, e.g. `continuedFrom: { sessionId, sessionTitle, version }` when the resolved artifact was created in another session, and let the model say so in its answer. In the panel, label the row with the creating session's title and put the per-version producer in the version menu (`v4 · 本会话 · 06:41`, `v3 · <session A> · 06:22`).
2. **Ask on the first cross-session write.** When the resolved artifact's `createdInSessionId` differs from the calling session, do not append silently: return a conflict that offers "continue this chain" (`baseVersionId` set, so CAS applies) or "publish as a new artifact" — the store already supports the latter as `forceNewArtifact` (`store.ts:5706`). The existing research-copy 409 gives the message shape to reuse.
3. Always require a base for a continuation, so a write that did not read the current version cannot overwrite it.

The project-level chain itself is intended (same path = same product inside one research scope) and should stay; what is missing is that the join is invisible and unavoidable.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Sessions: `fca861a5-…` (A, created `report.md` at 05:29), `e9afb9af-…` (B, published `v4` at 06:41). Container: `27cb6928-…`.

### Additional Information

- Found while exercising fault recovery (scenario S-203): the new session only wrote a run log named `report.md`, and was surprised by `version 4`.
- Related but separate: #1300 / #1301 (version numbers allocated without a uniqueness guard, and the stale-pointer allocation fix).
- The version picker itself (`v3`/`v2`/`v1` with no other identifier) was noted in #1300; this issue adds the missing provenance on top of it.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
1306.title: [Bug]: A new session silently continues an existing artifact version chain

1311.author: yuanzhou75
1311.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

The Idea Tree real-model L4 journey in #1293 passes only about half the time on the same commit. The failure is not in the assertion or the sandbox: the agent sometimes spends its whole preparation budget exploring the workspace and skill directories and never calls `create_idea_research`, so no research exists and the case fails waiting for the research card.

## Observed

Two runs, same head `a5f028cdad2a0a473b3c926704fc84f373f10d4f`, same prompt, same settings (water-treatment template, `quick`), same model:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | passed — `1 passed (8.2m)`, `playwright_exit=0` |
| 2 | failed — step 1 `getByRole('region', { name: 'Idea Tree 研究控制' })`, `Timeout: 180000ms exceeded`, `element(s) not found`, case body 3.2 min |

In the passing run the model called the tool after ~72s. In the failing run it was still exploring at round 4:

```
已探索 …
已调用 list_files            -> "Writable workspace is empty"
$SCIENCEDISCOVERY_SKILLS_DIR/structure-pocket-inspection
调用失败: run_shell          (mkdir -p /workspace/idea_tree && cat …)
Run stopped / Run cancelled
```

## What was ruled out

- **Not the sandbox.** The `run_shell` failure is a consequence of the cancellation, not its cause. The same command (`mkdir -p /workspace/idea_tree && echo ok && ls -la /workspace`) run standalone in a fresh session returns `status=succeeded`, exit 0, prints `ok`, and creates the directory.
- **Not the selector.** The passing run used the identical `getByRole('region', { name: 'Idea Tree 研究控制' })`.
- **Not the model endpoint.** Both runs used the same endpoint and model.

## Why it matters

The journey exists to prove that a live model starts an Idea Tree research **from the prompt itself** — `/idea-tree …` is deliberately not intercepted, so the agent has to call `create_idea_research` on its own (`apps/desktop/src/idea/command.ts`). That is exactly the step that intermittently does not happen. As a gate the case is unreliable at 1/2: it will fail PRs and nightly runs that have nothing wrong with them.

## Environment

WSL Ubuntu / linux-amd64; stack on the default `http://127.0.0.1:4310` with the repository-default data directory `.sciencediscovery-data` (`start-stack --mode local` reads the repository `.env`, which overrides an exported `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR`); real runner; bubblewrap 0.9.0; model `http://113.46.219.251:8080/v1` with `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`; backend `legacy` (`start-stack.sh --no-jiuwenswarm`, because that checkout fails the jiuwenswarm patch check).

## What is not yet established

Whether this is a prompt-shaping problem, ordinary model variance at the planning step, or a product defect in how the agent picks tools. No code change is implied by this report; a pass rate over several runs and the failing run's transcript are the next evidence to collect.

## Version Information

- Task under test: the real-model L4 Idea Tree journey added by #1293 (`test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts`).
- Test head: `a5f028cdad2a0a473b3c926704fc84f373f10d4f` (PR #1293), two runs on that same head.
- Product code under test: the Linux checkout in WSL, working tree synced to `main` on 2026-11-22 (the checkout's `.git` HEAD is stale because the tree is synced by tarball; the working tree is what ran).
- Desktop build 0.4.1 was **not** used for this reproduction.
- Model: `http://113.46.219.251:8080/v1` / `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`.
1311.title: [Bug]: Real L4 Idea Tree journey: the agent sometimes never calls create_idea_research

1313.author: yuanzhou75
1313.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees first:** one skill file with a broken frontmatter makes the API answer **HTTP 400 to every request**, including `GET /health`. The workbench becomes unusable (nothing loads), and any health probe — the desktop's readiness check, the E2E `requireRealStack` gate, a monitoring check — reports the service as broken, although the process is running and its data is intact.

**Measured.** A skill that is actually loaded (`skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md`, the file shipped in the repo) had an unquoted `description` containing `: `, which is invalid YAML. With that file in the tree:

```
$ curl -sS -m 3 -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4310/health
{"error":"SKILL.md frontmatter is invalid YAML: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:\n\ndescription: Use when the composer message starts with /idea-tree or /idea-tree-team, or the user explicitly asks for autonomous Idea Tree research: prepare supplied inputs for the research and explain its saved results.\n             ^\n"}
HTTP=400
```

- The same request **with** `Authorization: Bearer <token>` returns the identical body and `HTTP 400`.
- `HTTP 400`, not `503` and not a degraded payload: the failure is a refusal at the request entrance, before routing.
- The process had already logged `ScienceDiscovery listening on http://127.0.0.1:4310` and had served requests before the file was swapped in, so this is a **runtime, per-request** failure, not a startup crash.

**Negative control.** A newly added skill directory that is *not* loaded (a stray `skills/zz-bad-yaml-probe/SKILL.md` with the same kind of invalid YAML) did **not** break anything: `/health` kept answering `200`. So the trigger is "a skill the catalog actually loads", not "any YAML file under `skills/`".

**Expected.** A malformed skill file should be reported (logged, and once in the UI where skills are listed) and that **one** skill skipped; it must not take the whole API — and certainly not `/health` — down. `GET /health` should keep answering its normal payload, because a health probe must not depend on skill content.

**Reproduce**

1. Put the invalid frontmatter above into `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` (the description value unquoted, containing `: `).
2. Start the stack: `./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`.
3. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4310/health` → `HTTP 400` with the JSON error above.
4. Restore a valid file → `HTTP 200` with the normal health payload, no restart of anything else needed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- WSL Ubuntu 24.04 on Windows 11 (Chinese locale), linux-amd64, Node v22.
- Checkout: `sciencediscovery`, working tree synced to `main` (2026-11-22); the malformed file came from a PR head under review (`667368d7`), reproduced on that head.
- Stack: `./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`; API on `http://127.0.0.1:4310`, default data directory `.sciencediscovery-data`, real runner, bubblewrap 0.9.0.
- Reproduced twice: once incidentally while running a real E2E journey, once as this write-up's reproduction.
- Model endpoint is irrelevant to this defect (no model call is needed).

### Additional Information

- The error text is emitted by the skill-catalog load path; it names the offending file and the YAML line/column, so the loader already knows which file failed — the missing part is containing that failure to that one skill.
- Scope I verified directly: `GET /health`, authenticated and not. Because the refusal happens at the request entrance (the same body is returned for a route that must never read skills), I expect other routes are equally affected, but I did not probe them one by one — that part is inference, not measurement.
- Suggested acceptance: a malformed skill file is logged and skipped; `/health` still answers 200; the skills list shows that one skill as failed rather than the catalog being empty; and a test feeds the loader an invalid frontmatter and asserts the API still answers `/health`.
- This is a product defect and is independent of the PR that happened to contain the malformed file (that PR only edits prose in a skill description).

### Version Information

- Product code under test: repo `main` working tree synced 2026-11-22 (the checkout is synced by tarball, so its `.git` HEAD is stale; the working tree is what ran).
- Malformed file provenance: PR head `667368d7` (fixed later at `e4410b80`, which parses cleanly).
- No desktop build was involved: the defect reproduces over the HTTP API alone.
1313.title: [Bug]: one skill file with invalid frontmatter makes every API route return 400, including /health
